title: Ten bridesmaids and a long night
hymns: 390~Praise to the Lord, the Almighty~Entrance|423~Immortal, Invisible, God Only Wise~Gradual|396~Now Thank We All Our God~Closing
summary: The parable of the ten bridesmaids is not about who is good and who is bad. It is about oil, which is to say about what cannot be borrowed at the last minute.
body:
Every one of the ten bridesmaids falls asleep. That is the detail I want to start with this morning, because we usually skip it. The wise ones are not the ones who stay awake. Nobody stays awake. The bridegroom is late, the night is long, and all ten of them nod off with their lamps beside them.

What separates them is the oil. Five of them brought extra, and five did not, and when the shout goes up at midnight it turns out that oil is one of the things you cannot hand to someone else. You cannot borrow a habit of prayer. You cannot borrow the friendships you did not make, or the forgiveness you did not practice.

So the question this parable puts to a parish is not whether we are awake enough. It is what we are storing up for the long night: the small, unglamorous things, the Tuesday Bible study, the casserole list, the pantry shift, that will still be burning when we need them.

title: What were you given, and what did you do with it?
hymns: 401~The God of Abraham Praise~Entrance|518~Christ Is Made the Sure Foundation~Gradual|488~Be Thou My Vision~Closing
summary: A talent was about twenty years of wages. The parable is not about spare change; it is about being trusted with a great deal, and what fear does to us when we are.
body:
A talent in Jesus' day was not a skill. It was a weight of silver worth something like twenty years of a laborer's wages. The master in the story hands out fortunes, and then leaves.

The third servant is not lazy. He is afraid. He says so: I knew you were a harsh man, so I was afraid, and I went and hid your talent in the ground. Fear makes him bury the very thing he was trusted with.

This is the Sunday our parish talks about pledges, and I want to say plainly that this sermon is not a fundraising appeal. It is a question about fear. What have we buried because we were afraid of losing it? A gift for music, a hard conversation, a building that could do more for this town than it does on a Tuesday afternoon?

title: The king who was hungry
hymns: 494~Crown Him with Many Crowns~Entrance|460~Alleluia! Sing to Jesus~Gradual|376~Joyful, Joyful, We Adore Thee~Closing
summary: On the last Sunday of the church year we crown Christ as king, and the Gospel shows us where to find him: hungry, thirsty, a stranger, sick and in prison.
body:
We end the church year with a coronation. Crown Him with Many Crowns, the white and gold back on the altar, a feast that sounds like it belongs in a cathedral.

And then the Gospel. The king in Matthew 25 is not found on a throne. He is found in a queue at the Ferry Street Pantry on a Thursday afternoon. He is the man in the hospital bed on the fourth floor of Wend Valley General who has not had a visitor since August.

Neither the sheep nor the goats knew who they were serving. That is the part that should comfort us and unsettle us in equal measure. Next week the color changes to blue and we start waiting again. This week, look around the room you are standing in.

title: The guest list
hymns: 390~Praise to the Lord, the Almighty~Entrance|423~Immortal, Invisible, God Only Wise~Gradual|657~Love Divine, All Loves Excelling~Closing
summary: The parable of the wedding banquet, where the invited guests are too busy and the servants are sent out to the street corners.
body:
Everybody on the first guest list has a reason not to come. A field, a business, a new marriage. None of them are bad reasons. That is what makes the parable uncomfortable.

The banquet goes ahead anyway, with whoever is standing on the street corner. Our church supper on Thursday will be a little like that, and I hope it is.

title: Whose image is this?
hymns: 401~The God of Abraham Praise~Entrance|518~Christ Is Made the Sure Foundation~Gradual|396~Now Thank We All Our God~Closing
summary: Give to the emperor what is the emperor's. The coin has Caesar's face on it. What has God's?
body:
The question is a trap and Jesus knows it. Pay the tax and you are a collaborator; refuse and you are a rebel. So he asks for a coin, and asks whose face is on it.

The answer is Caesar's. And then the question nobody asks out loud: whose image is on you? Genesis has already answered that. We are coins stamped with somebody else's face.

title: The great commandment, on a Monday
hymns: 390~Praise to the Lord, the Almighty~Entrance|518~Christ Is Made the Sure Foundation~Gradual|657~Love Divine, All Loves Excelling~Closing
summary: Love God, love your neighbor. Everybody agrees with it on Sunday. The deacon's sermon is about what it looks like at work on Monday morning.
body:
I spend my weekdays as a hospital chaplain, so I hear the great commandment at three in the morning more often than I hear it on Sunday.

Love of neighbor at three in the morning looks like a nurse who refills the water jug without being asked. It is that small, and that large.

title: A great multitude that no one could count
hymns: 287~For All the Saints~Entrance|460~Alleluia! Sing to Jesus~Gradual|488~Be Thou My Vision~Closing
summary: We read aloud the names of everyone from the parish who died this year, and remember that the communion of saints is larger than the room.
body:
This morning we will read forty-one names. Some of them sat in these pews for sixty years. Some of them we only met at the end, in a hospital room or a hospice bed.

Revelation imagines a crowd from every nation, tribe, people and language, too many to count. Our forty-one names are a very small part of that crowd, and a very precious one.
